ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that $AB\parallel CD$, and the line $MN$ intersects $AB$ and $CD$ at points $E$ and $F$ respectively, and $\angle NEB=58^\circ$. What is the degree measure of $\angle CFE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $\angle NEB$ and $\angle AEF$ are vertical angles, and $\angle NEB=58^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle AEF=\angle NEB=58^\circ$.\\
Since $AB \parallel CD$,\\
we have $\angle AEF + \angle CFE = 180^\circ$,\\
therefore $\angle CFE = 180^\circ - 58^\circ = \boxed{122^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are two mutually parallel straight lines AB and CD; the straight line MN, as a transversal, intersects AB and CD at E and F respectively. Point E is on the straight line AB, and point F is on the straight line CD; ray EN and EF are opposite rays on the same straight line MN, and ray EB and EA are opposite rays on the straight line AB. The problem gives ∠NEB = 58°. Reasoning: Because ∠NEB and ∠AEF are vertical angles formed by the intersection of the two straight lines MN and AB, ∠AEF = ∠NEB = 58°. Also because AB ∥ CD and EF is a transversal, ∠AEF and ∠CFE are same-side interior angles, and their sum is 180°. Therefore ∠CFE = 180° - 58° = 122°.
